hook: The lame conqueror of Central Asia, builder of Samarkand and destroyer of cities.

pages.x: Timur was born in 1336 near Samarkand, into a Turkic Mongol clan. As a young man, raiding sheep, he was hit by arrows in his right leg and hand, leaving him lame for life. Persians called him Timur-i Lang, "Timur the Lame", which Europeans turned into Tamerlane.

From 1370 he spent 35 years at war. He conquered Persia, Iraq and the Caucasus, crushed the Golden Horde, and sacked Delhi in 1398 and Damascus and Baghdad in 1401. His empire stretched from Turkey to India.

He terrified cities into surrender. Those that resisted were slaughtered and their skulls piled into towers: perhaps 70,000 at Isfahan in 1387. His wars may have killed 17 million people, around one in twenty of everyone alive at the time.
In 1402 at Ankara he crushed the Ottoman army and captured Sultan Bayezid. Legend says he kept the sultan in an iron cage and used him as a footstool. Bayezid died in captivity a few months later.
He brought artists, builders and scholars from conquered lands to make his capital, Samarkand, the most beautiful city in Asia, with blue-tiled domes and the vast Bibi-Khanym Mosque.

He died in 1405 on his way to invade China. Legend says his tomb warned that whoever opened it would unleash an invader worse than him. Soviet scientists opened it on 19 June 1941. Three days later, Hitler invaded the Soviet Union.

Timur was the last great conqueror of the steppe, a builder of splendid cities and destroyer of many more. His descendants founded the Mughal Empire in India, and Uzbekistan honours him as a national hero.
pts: Conquered an empire from Turkey to India
Made Samarkand a city of blue domes
His descendants founded the Mughal Empire
